title: kv-cache: defragmentation, paging spillover and eviction policy improvements
author: Sasha Patel
body: Motivation: We see increased memory fragmentation in the KV cache under mixed-length chat workloads which causes premature evictions and higher tail latency. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) a background defragmentation/compaction pass that coalesces free spans inside the in-memory slab allocator to reduce external fragmentation; 2) a paging/spillover path that asynchronously moves cold KV segments to a local fast-persistent store (memfd-backed file or tmpfs-mounted spill file) to avoid OOMs without blocking hot requests; 3) improved eviction policy that combines a segmented-LRU with a size-aware admission heuristic and a per-shard hot-score so we avoid evicting large, frequently accessed KV blobs. The body contains an implementation summary, testing, and rollout plan. Implementation summary: Defragmentation is implemented as a low-priority background worker per-shard that scans free lists and uses a relocation protocol to move live KV entries into compacted spans while keeping per-request latencies bounded. We added safe double-buffering so readers may still access entries while they are relocated; relocation commits are serialized via a shard-level epoch. Paging/spillover: when shard free bytes dip below a dynamic threshold we asynchronously serialize cold entries to a spill file using a configurable compression codec (none/snappy) and mark entries as paged-out. Page-in is lazy and prioritized for requests that hit paged keys. The spill file is managed as an append-only segment store with a small LRU index to bound memory. Eviction policy: the existing global LRU was causing churn on short-lived keys and large KV blobs. We added a segmented policy: tiny/short-lived segment for conversational prefixes, medium segment for recent responses, and a protected hot segment for pinned/hot keys (heuristic from recent access frequency and token coverage). Evictions prefer entries from the tiny/short segment and use size-aware scoring to avoid purging a single large KV entry that would cause expensive re-population. Metrics and observability: new metrics exported per-shard: kv_defrag_runs_total, kv_defrag_moved_bytes, kv_spill_segments_total, kv_page_ins_total/kv_page_outs_total, kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_eviction_score_histogram. Instrumentation added to the console and per-route dashboards. Testing and benchmarks: added unit tests covering relocation correctness, page-in/out race conditions, and recovery after crash during spill segment write. Microbenchmarks show 18-28% reduction in tail latency P95/P99 for mixed-length chat traces and a 30% drop in eviction rate on heavy prefix workloads. Rollout plan: start with feature-flag disabled by default. Gradually enable defrag-only on a small set of shards, then enable spillover for low-priority tenants, and finally ramp the combined policy cluster-wide if metrics look good. Migration notes and config knobs: new runtime flags kv.defrag.enabled, kv.defrag.max_bytes_per_cycle, kv.spill.enabled, kv.spill.compression, kv.eviction.size_bias, kv.eviction.hot_score_window_ms. Backwards compatibility: on rolling upgrade the spill file format is versioned; older nodes ignore paged entries and will cause a page-in on access which is safe. Related work: follows up on earlier spillover and defrag PRs pr-35821, pr-33127 and references Linear ENG-5421 for the eviction policy design. Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] Perf benchmark harness updates - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated - [x] Feature flags added - [x] Safety migration path and docs Changeset overview: modified allocator and shard runtime, added defrag worker, added spill segment manager and serializer, updated eviction scorer and admission heuristics, console metric wiring, added tests, and examples.

review_comments: Miguel Rivera: Overall this looks solid. Two concerns: 1) we need stronger bounds on defrag CPU usage; 2) ensure spill file corruption is detected and triggers safe fallback.
Author (Sasha): Added cpu throttling knobs and a checksum/version header for spill files. Also added recovery unit tests.
Priya Sharma: Please add more observability for page-in latency so customers can correlate page-in events with tail spikes.
Author (Sasha): Added kv_page_in_latency_ms histogram and console panels.
Evan Cho: Approve after addressing a minor concurrency comment in allocator.h
ci_summary: CI: unit tests passed, integration tests flaky on spill_recovery in first run and rerun succeeded. Lint passes. Perf job ran and produced regression-free numbers. All checks green.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory usage by adding defragmentation, introduces configurable spillover to a local spill file to avoid OOMs, and refines eviction policy to reduce unnecessary evictions and tail latency. Feature gated and rolled out gradually.
notes_for_ops: Ops: enable behind feature flags. Start with kv.defrag.enabled=true and kv.spill.enabled=false, watch kv_fragmentation_ratio and kv_eviction_rate. If using spill, set kv.spill.compression=snappy for lower IO. The spill file path and retention are configurable; ensure enough local disk and liveness of cleanup task. Rolling back requires disabling spill and allowing paged entries to be paged-in; we included a compatibility header so old nodes will page-in transparently.
benchmark_results: Mixed chat benchmark (trace v2026-01): baseline P95 112ms -> 92ms (-18%), P99 278ms -> 201ms (-28%). Eviction rate decreased from 0.43 ops/s to 0.30 ops/s in steady-state long-lived sessions.
changelog_entry: kv-cache: defragmentation + spillover + improved eviction policy (feature-gated)
author_notes: Will monitor kv_fragmentation_ratio and kv_page_in_latency_ms closely during rollout. Follow-up work: remote tiering for spill segments and adaptive compression selection based on workload.
